messages:
maya: FYI Acme reported intermittent 500/502s from their Dedicated EU pool hitting /v1/generate since ~09:11UTC. Customer sent request_id=8f3a2b1c and a curl that reproduces a backend error. Can someone grab pod logs + GPU metrics from the eu-dedicated node they were routed to?

josh: Which pod/node are they on?

maya: Pod name: inference-7b-xyz-5f7d (namespace: dedicated-eu-03). Node: eu-dedicated-7 (ip 10.10.7.23). Labels: tenant=acme, pool=reserved-eu. Customer-supplied curl:```curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwkv-13b-quant","input":"<snipped>","max_tokens":512}'```

maya: Gateway logs show backend returned 502 then 500 for that request_id:```[2026-03-17T09:11:42Z] request_id=8f3a2b1c svc=inference handler=generate status=502 latency=3401ms details="runner timeout waiting for kv flush"
[2026-03-17T09:11:43Z] request_id=8f3a2b9d svc=inference handler=generate status=500 latency=12002ms details="process died during generation"```

josh: Can you run these on the node/pod and paste outputs?
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu-03 get pods -o wide | grep inference-7b-xyz
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu-03 logs inference-7b-xyz-5f7d -c runner --since=30m
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu-03 exec inference-7b-xyz-5f7d -c runner -- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION --format=csv
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu-03 exec inference-7b-xyz-5f7d -c runner -- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/errata || true

maya: Running now, pasting important bits. Pod list:```inference-7b-xyz-5f7d   1/1 Running   2 (5m ago)   10.10.73.12   eu-dedicated-7```

Logs (runner, tail):```2026-03-17T09:10:58Z INFO start generation request_id=8f3a2b1c tenant=acme model=rwkv-13b-quant batch_size=1
2026-03-17T09:11:40Z WARN kv_cache flush took 1800ms request_id=8f3a2b1c
2026-03-17T09:11:42Z ERROR uncaught exception request_id=8f3a2b1c trace='segfault in cuda driver'
2026-03-17T09:11:42Z INFO process restart scheduled pid=34567
2026-03-17T09:11:43Z ERROR generation failed request_id=8f3a2b9d cause='process died'```

nvidia-smi excerpt:```GPU 0: name=H100-SXM4, memory.total=81GiB, memory.used=81GiB, utilization.gpu=99%
Processes: python (pid=34567)  GPU Memory Usage: 78.3GiB
ECC Errors: 0 Corrected, 4 Uncorrectable
Temperature: 72C```

dcgm-exporter (recent):```{"gpu":0,"util":98,"mem_used":78832,"pstate":0,"pci_ecc_uncorrectable":4}```

infra-bot: Reminder: use ri-cli collect-debug-bundle to get consistent bundle. Example:```ri-cli collect-debug-bundle --tenant acme --request 8f3a2b1c --nodes eu-dedicated-7 --out /tmp/acme-8f3a-debug.tar.gz```

devex-bot: Also include kernel logs and container runtime logs:```journalctl -k --since "2026-03-17 09:00" > /tmp/dmesg.log; journalctl -u containerd --since "2026-03-17 09:00" > /tmp/containerd.log```

anika: I can take this. Please upload the bundle to a presigned S3 link and drop it here. Also include the exact SDK call (sdk version + tokenization length) and whether batching or prefix cache was enabled.

maya: Uploading now. Files collected: /tmp/inference.log, /tmp/dmesg.log, /tmp/nvidia-smi.txt, /tmp/dcgm.json, /tmp/containerd.log. Presigned link (24h): https://presigned.s3/acme/8f3a-debug-2026.tar.gz

anika: Downloaded bundle and doing a quick triage. Early indicators: GPU memory saturated + several uncorrectable ECC events around the same timestamps. Kernel shows PCIe link reset followed by "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" messages (different Xid than previous incidents). Containerd shows the runner process was OOM-killed inside the container before a graceful shutdown. Opening INC-1124 and assigning to eng-runtime.

josh: Can you confirm whether batch size or cache flush patterns changed for this tenant recently? Might be a burst of short requests causing full KV memory retention.

maya: Customer says they disabled batching yesterday to reduce latency. Payloads are ~420 tokens (tokenized). SDK: rw-sdk-js v2.4.1. They called /v1/generate with streaming disabled, so runner kept full KV in memory for each request.

anika: That explains sustained memory pressure. Short-term mitigation: re-enable batching or route tenant to a variant with smaller kv (rwkv-13b-quant-small-kv) or increase reserved GPU capacity. I'll prepare a canary plan to route their traffic to a fallback model for 10 minutes to confirm.

anika: Action items: 1) maya upload full bundle to INC-1124 (done), 2) josh capture node-level perf metrics for 09:00-09:20 window (iostat, sar, nvidia-smi history) and attach to ticket, 3) devex prepare a safe fallback launch (model variant with smaller KV) and a routing policy change.

maya: Uploaded node metrics and ticket updated.

josh: I grabbed node perf: PCIe errors spike at 09:11, GPU mem pressure transitions map to the request ids. Putting logs in INC-1124.

anika: I'll implement a temporary routing rule to send tenant=acme to rwkv-13b-quant-small-kv for 10 minutes and monitor. If stable, we recommend customer re-enable batching or we propose a reserved capacity increase.

maya: Thanks all — customer notified of mitigation and we'll update when canary completes. :thumbsup:
